\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Bounded-time machine behavior]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NGood}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NGood}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $K$ work tapes, and let $C$ be a
configuration on input $x$. For a time bound $T$ and predicates $	ext{box}$ and $Q$ on
configurations, every choice string of length at most $T$ must lead to a configuration
satisfying $	ext{box}$; moreover, every choice string of length exactly $T$ must lead to
a halted configuration satisfying $Q$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Halting makes a choice suffix irrelevant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.runWith_append_of_halt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.runWith_append_of_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_of_halt}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine, $C$ a configuration on a fixed
input, and $u,v$ finite Boolean words. If running from $C$ under the choice word $u$
reaches a halted configuration, then running from $C$ under the concatenated choice word
$uv$ yields the same configuration as running under $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Implication for the Terminal Property]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.imp}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.imp}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NGood, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine, let $C$ be a configuration, let $T$ be a
natural number, and let $\mathrm{box}$, $Q$, and $Q'$ be properties of configurations.
Suppose all runs from $C$ of length at most $T$ end in configurations satisfying
$\mathrm{box}$, and every run of length exactly $T$ ends in a halted configuration
satisfying $Q$. If every configuration satisfying $Q$ also satisfies $Q'$, then every
run of length exactly $T$ ends in a halted configuration satisfying $Q'$, and all runs
of length at most $T$ still satisfy $\mathrm{box}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of good runs]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.mono}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NGood, Complexity.LogProg.runWith_append_of_halt, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic machine, $C$ an initial configuration, and $T \le T'$
natural numbers. If every choice word of length at most $T$ leads from $C$ to a
configuration satisfying $\mathrm{box}$, and every choice word of length exactly $T$
leads to a halted configuration satisfying $Q$, then the same properties hold with $T'$
in place of $T$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenating good run segments]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.seg}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.seg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NGood, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic machine, let $C,C'$ be configurations, and let $S,T$ be
natural numbers. Suppose every run from $C$ of length at most $S$ satisfies
$\mathrm{box}$, and every run from $C$ of length exactly $S$ ends at $C'$. If every run
from $C'$ of length at most $T$ satisfies $\mathrm{box}$ and every run from $C'$ of
length exactly $T$ is halted and satisfies $Q$, then every run from $C$ of length at
most $S+T$ satisfies $\mathrm{box}$, and every run from $C$ of length exactly $S+T$ is
halted and satisfies $Q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Goodness After a Nondeterministic Choice]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.choose}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NGood.choose}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NGood, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $N$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine, let $C$ be a configuration, let $T$ be a
natural number, and let $\mathrm{box}$ and $Q$ be properties of configurations. Suppose
$\mathrm{box}(C)$ holds, and that for each choice bit $b$, one step from $C$ under $b$
yields $C_b$, from which all runs of length at most $T$ end in configurations satisfying
$\mathrm{box}$, while every run of length exactly $T$ ends in a halted configuration
satisfying $Q$. Then all runs from $C$ of length at most $T+1$ end in configurations
satisfying $\mathrm{box}$, and every run of length exactly $T+1$ ends in a halted
configuration satisfying $Q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Guarded nondeterministic program configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NGuard}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NGuard}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NPre, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
For an NARM $A$, an oracle, a multi-tape machine $D$, a state assignment $q_0$,
natural-number bounds $B,W$, a Boolean input $x$, and an abstract configuration $a$,
define the guard condition to hold when $NPre(A,\mathrm{oracle},D,q_0,B,x,a)$ holds and,
for every register $r$, the binary representation of the register value plus one has
length at most $W$ (that is, $|(\mathrm{bits}(a_r+1))|\le W$).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Simulation of a Nondeterministic Register Program]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_run}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NBox, Complexity.LogProg.NGood, Complexity.LogProg.NGood.choose, Complexity.LogProg.NGood.imp, Complexity.LogProg.NGood.mono, Complexity.LogProg.NGood.seg, Complexity.LogProg.NGuard, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.guard, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.of_choose, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.of_det, Complexity.LogProg.aseam, Complexity.LogProg.astep_cases, Complexity.LogProg.nans_choose, Complexity.LogProg.nans_det, Complexity.LogProg.nans_halted, Complexity.LogProg.nbox_seam, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileTM, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileTM_stepWith_choose, Complexity.LogProg.ndet_halt, Complexity.LogProg.ndet_live, Complexity.LogProg.runWith_append_of_halt, Complexity.LogProg.seam, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons}
\difficulty{6}
Fix nonnegative integers $m,d,k_D$, sets $\Lambda,SD$, an input bit string $x$, a
nondeterministic register program $A$ with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle choices, an
initial location $l_0$, an oracle, a deterministic $k_D$-tape machine $D$, initial
decider states $q_0(j)$, and bounds $B,W$. For every $N\ge 0$, location $l\in\Lambda$,
register valuation $v:\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\to\mathbb N$, and output bit string
$\mathrm{out}$, suppose every length-$N$ choice string makes the program halt from
configuration $(l,v,\text{no answer})$, and every configuration before halting satisfies
the guard requiring the deterministic preconditions and the register bit-length bounds
by $W$. Then there is a time $T$ such that, from the compiled machine configuration
corresponding to $(l,v,\mathrm{out})$, every choice string of length at most $T$ yields
a configuration whose first $m$ work-tape heads stay between $-1$ and $W$ and whose
remaining work-tape heads stay within distance $B$ of zero; every choice string of
length exactly $T$ yields a halting configuration whose output is $\mathrm{out}$
followed by an answer attainable by the register program in $N$ choices. Moreover, for
every answer attainable by the register program in $N$ choices, some length-$T$ choice
string makes the compiled machine output $\mathrm{out}$ followed by that answer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space bound for compiled nondeterministic programs]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_space}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_space}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NGuard, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.aseam, Complexity.LogProg.narm_run, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileFinNDTM, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileTM, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileTM_init, Complexity.LogProg.seam, Complexity.LogProg.spaceUsedWith_le_of_ranges, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with initial label $l_0$, oracle, and
decider machine $D$ with initial states $q_0$, and let $B,W,N$ be natural numbers.
Suppose every sequence of $N$ choice bits makes the program halt, and each configuration
before halting satisfies the guard: its applicable instruction preconditions hold, every
decider call has distinct argument registers and a clean run using at most $B$ work-head
cells, and each register value $z$ satisfies $|\text{the binary length of }z+1|\le W$.
Then there is a number $T$ such that the compiled machine halts for every length-$T$
choice sequence and uses at most $m(W+2)+k_D(2B+1)$ work-tape cells on each such run.
Moreover, there exists a length-$N$ choice sequence on which the register program's
answer is true if and only if the compiled machine has an accepting run of length $T$.
\end{theorem}
